title: Keeping The Wide Full-Court View During Live Passing and Dribbling
trigger_condition: The ball is live and players are dribbling, passing, and moving to set up a shot.
editor_action: Stay on CAM-1 (Main Wide) so anyone watching can see all 10 players at once, understand who is open, and follow where the ball is moving. Never cut to a tight close-up of a single face or the bench while the ball is in play.
timing_constraint: Hold the wide camera continuously until a basket is made or a whistle stops play, especially when the shot timer is running out (example: final 7s on the shot clock).
plain_english_tip: Two Clocks: Teams have 30 seconds on the shot clock to hit the rim on each possession while the 20-minute half clock counts down.

title: Full-Game Camera Balance: Why The Wide Court View Stays on Most of The Time
trigger_condition: Macro Game Pattern (Full 60-Minute Broadcast Arc): Balancing how much total time viewers spend on the wide full-court camera versus close-up player, bench, and replay cameras.
editor_action: Keep CAM-1 (the elevated wide center-court camera) on screen for roughly two-thirds to three-quarters of the entire broadcast (~68% to 74%) so even someone brand new to basketball can always tell which hoop each team is attacking and where all 10 players are standing. Use close-up and replay cameras as brief punctuation marks: CAM-3 (Player Close-Up) Player Close-Up (~12% to 15%), Slow-Motion Replays (~10% to 12%), CAM-4 (Coach & Bench) Coach & Bench (~5% to 7%), CAM-2 (Baseline Low) Under-Basket Low (~4% to 6%), and CAM-5 (Above-Rim) Overhead Rim (~1% to 2%).
timing_constraint: Full-game camera share: Wide CAM-1 (~68-74%), Player CAM-3 (~12-15%), Replays (~10-12%), Coach CAM-4 (~5-7%), Baseline CAM-2 (~4-6%), Overhead CAM-5 (~1-2%).

title: Never Switching Cameras While a Shot Is Flying Through The Air
trigger_condition: A player shoots the basketball (especially a long 3-point shot) and the ball is currently in mid-air traveling toward the hoop.
editor_action: Keep the camera completely still on CAM-1 (Main Wide) until the ball either goes through the net or bounces off the rim. Switching to a close-up camera while the ball is in the air disorients viewers because they cannot see whether the shot went in.
timing_constraint: Zero camera cuts from the moment the shooter releases the ball until the make or rebound outcome is clear (example: wait 0.3s to 0.4s after the swish before cutting to CAM-3).
plain_english_tip: 3-Pointer: Any shot released from behind the large painted arc counts for 3 points instead of 2.

title: Locking The Wide Camera When The 30-Second Shot Timer Runs Low
trigger_condition: The offense has been passing and dribbling for over 20 seconds and has only a few seconds left on the 30-second shot timer to release a shot.
editor_action: Lock the broadcast on CAM-1 (Main Wide) so viewers can see the entire court, spot whether anyone is open, and watch the buzzer-beating shot attempt. Never cut to a close-up camera when the shot timer is winding down.
timing_constraint: Strict wide-camera lock whenever the shot timer drops into the final seconds of a possession (example: final 7 to 8 seconds on the shot clock).
plain_english_tip: Two Clocks: Teams have 30 seconds on the shot clock to hit the rim on each possession while the 20-minute half clock counts down.

title: Respectful Wide Camera Takeover When a Player Is Injured on The Court (Safety Rule)
trigger_condition: A player falls hard, is hurt on the court, or medical trainers are called onto the floor.
editor_action: Immediately switch to the wide full-court view (CAM-1, Main Wide) or the team bench (CAM-4, Coach & Bench) and keep it there. Never zoom in on an injured player in pain, and block all slow-motion replays of the injury out of respect for the student-athlete (CUJ 1.4).
timing_constraint: Immediate wide-camera lock for the entire duration of the medical stoppage until the player is safely up and play resumes.

title: Automatic Backup Camera Switch If a Camera Signal Glitches
trigger_condition: The active camera feed experiences sustained video breakup, freezing, or static lasting longer than a single frame (CUJ 1.1).
editor_action: Ignore a tiny one-frame flicker so the viewer isn't jarred by an unnecessary cut, but if a camera signal breaks up for roughly a second or more, automatically switch to a clean backup camera (such as CAM-2 (Baseline Low) Baseline) until the main wide camera signal is clean again.
timing_constraint: Switch to a clean backup angle whenever signal breakup persists past a brief moment, and return to CAM-1 once stable (example: >1.0s glitch failover).

title: Pre-Cut Camera Stability Gate (Never Cut to a Whip-Panning or Blurry Camera)
trigger_condition: An isolation camera (CAM-2, CAM-3, or CAM-4) is still rapidly swinging ('whip-panning'), zooming, or hunting for focus to find a player after a basket or whistle.
editor_action: Cutting to a camera while it is still jerking across the court or blurry makes viewers dizzy. Always verify that the target camera has locked onto the player and held a steady, focused frame for a brief beat before switching it onto the live broadcast.
timing_constraint: Require a steady, settled camera frame before executing the switch (example: 0.3s to 0.5s of stable framing with low pan velocity before cut).

title: Live-Camera Occlusion Auto-Eject (When a Fan or Referee Walks in Front of The Lens)
trigger_condition: An isolation camera (CAM-2 Baseline or CAM-3 Sideline Close-Up) is currently live on air, and a standing fan, referee, or player walks directly in front of the camera lens, blocking the view.
editor_action: Immediately bail out from the blocked camera back to CAM-1 (Main Wide) within a sub-second reaction window rather than leaving a blocked or blurry back-of-a-head view on television.
timing_constraint: Execute emergency fallback cut to CAM-1 Wide within a sub-second beat of severe lens occlusion (example: 0.4s to 0.6s bailout).

title: Blocked Shot Kept In-Bounds (Stay Locked on CAM-1 Wide)
trigger_condition: A defender blocks a shot, but the ball stays in bounds and triggers a live loose-ball scramble or fast break.
editor_action: Suppress all close-up reaction cuts on the shot-blocker and stay 100% locked on CAM-1 (Main Wide) because play is still live and transitioning downcourt.
timing_constraint: Zero cutaway; maintain continuous CAM-1 Wide coverage (Execute within <= 1.0s reaction window and return to CAM-1 before live ball.)
plain_english_tip: Fast Break & Press: Sprinting to score before defenders set up, or guarding full-court immediately after a made basket.

title: Final Free-Throw Intentional Miss Setup (Wide 10-Player Framing)
trigger_condition: A trailing team is down by 2 or 3 points in the final 10 seconds with 1 free throw remaining and no timeouts, where the shooter must intentionally miss the shot so teammates can tip it in.
editor_action: Lock onto CAM-1 (Main Wide) before the free throw is released so viewers can see the intentional brick off the front rim and the frantic rebound scramble.
timing_constraint: Lock CAM-1 Wide at least 2.0s before the final free-throw release.
plain_english_tip: Offensive Rebound: Catching your own team's missed shot resets the NCAA shot clock to 20 seconds for an extra scoring chance.

title: Full-Court Baseball Pass Inbound (Extra-Wide CAM-1 Framing)
trigger_condition: With under 5 seconds left in a half or game, a team inbounds from under its own basket needing to throw a long 'baseball pass' the length of the court.
editor_action: Zoom CAM-1 (Main Wide) out to its widest possible field of view centered near mid-court so both the inbounder's throw and the catch near the far 3-point line are captured in one continuous shot.
timing_constraint: Establish maximum-width CAM-1 framing 3.0s before the end-of-period throw-in.
plain_english_tip: 10-Second Backcourt: The offense has 10 seconds to dribble across the center line and cannot pass back behind it once across.

title: Half-Court Heave at The Buzzer: Track from Release to Backboard
trigger_condition: With under 2 seconds left in the 1st Half or 2nd Half, a player heaves a desperation shot from near mid-court.
editor_action: Pan and widen CAM-1 (Main Wide) smoothly with the flight of the ball so both the red backboard LED lights and the basket rim are clearly visible when the ball arrives.
timing_constraint: Hold continuous CAM-1 pan from mid-court release through rim contact + 2.0s.
plain_english_tip: 10-Second Backcourt: The offense has 10 seconds to dribble across the center line and cannot pass back behind it once across.

title: Goal-Line / Under-Basket Inbound Stack Formation (Stay on CAM-1)
trigger_condition: An offensive team lines up 4 players in a tight 'stack' or 'box' formation in the painted lane for a baseline inbound play under their own basket.
editor_action: Always use CAM-1 (Main Wide) rather than CAM-2 (Baseline Low) for baseline inbound plays because players cut in four directions at once and CAM-2 (Baseline Low) is too tight to see the open corner or lob pass.
timing_constraint: Lock CAM-1 Wide at least 1.5s before the referee hands the ball to the baseline inbounder.
plain_english_tip: The Paint: The rectangular lane under the hoop where inside scorers battle (offensive players cannot camp inside it for >3 seconds).

title: Overtime Opening Tip-Off Center-Circle Reframe
trigger_condition: Both teams line up around the center circle for the opening jump ball of a 5-minute Overtime period.
editor_action: Frame CAM-1 (Main Wide) centered on mid-court showing all 10 players and the referee's toss, holding CAM-1 (Main Wide) continuously through the tip and first offensive possession.
timing_constraint: Lock centered CAM-1 Wide 5.0s before the overtime jump ball.
plain_english_tip: 10-Second Backcourt: The offense has 10 seconds to dribble across the center line and cannot pass back behind it once across.

title: Cutting Back Immediately When The Other Team Rushes The Ball Inbounds (Fast-Inbound Rule)
trigger_condition: Right after a basket is made, the team that was scored on grabs the ball and throws it back onto the court immediately to start a fast break.
editor_action: Generalizes the post-basket celebration rule: while a normal celebration close-up lasts a couple of seconds when players jog slowly, a sub-second cut (or staying on the wide camera) is required whenever the other team pushes a fast inbound so viewers never miss a fast break.
timing_constraint: Sub-second celebration cut is allowed on a fast inbound before snapping back to CAM-1 Wide (example: 0.7s to 0.8s glance).
plain_english_tip: Fast Break & Press: Sprinting to score before defenders set up, or guarding full-court immediately after a made basket.

title: Pre-Tip-Off Center-Circle Jump Ball Framing
trigger_condition: The two starting centers step into the center circle at midcourt for the opening tip-off. (Visual cue: Referee standing between the two jumpers holding the basketball ready to toss; Audio cue: Arena PA announcer and starting buzzer/whistle.)
editor_action: Center CAM-1 (Main Wide) squarely on the midcourt circle with all 10 players visible around the circle so the viewer sees both the vertical leap and which team controls the tip (example: symmetrical midcourt framing before the toss). Recommended framing: Main Sideline Camera (CAM-1, Main Wide).
timing_constraint: Target window: symmetrical midcourt framing before the toss. Pan immediately in the direction the ball is tipped as soon as a player taps it.
plain_english_tip: 10-Second Backcourt: The offense has 10 seconds to dribble across the center line and cannot pass back behind it once across.

title: Ball-In-Frame Continuity Across Live Cut
trigger_condition: An emergency or rare camera switch occurs while the basketball is live on the court. (Visual cue: The basketball is being dribbled or passed in the outgoing camera frame; Audio cue: Live play-by-play narration.)
editor_action: Verify that the basketball is clearly visible inside the incoming camera frame before executing any live cut so the viewer never has to hunt across the screen to find where the ball went (example: 100% ball visibility in both outgoing and incoming frames). Recommended framing: Main Sideline Camera (CAM-1, Main Wide).
timing_constraint: Target window: 100% ball visibility in both outgoing and incoming frames. Never cut to a secondary camera during live play if the ball is outside that camera's field of view.

title: Theme Music Fade-Out on Live Inbound Pass
trigger_condition: The broadcast returns from a commercial break with the network's signature basketball theme music playing over a wide arena shot. (Visual cue: Players stepping onto the court and the referee handing the ball to the inbounder; Audio cue: Upbeat orchestral or hip-hop network broadcast theme music.)
editor_action: Fade the network theme music completely out before the ball is passed inbounds so the live game sounds and play-by-play call take center stage the instant live basketball resumes (example: smooth ~1.5s fade-out completing before the inbound pass). Recommended framing: Main Sideline Camera (CAM-1, Main Wide).
timing_constraint: Target window: smooth ~1.5s fade-out completing before the inbound pass. Never allow theme music to keep playing over a live possession.

title: Free-Throw Routine Waist-Up to Wide Release Sequence
trigger_condition: A player steps to the free-throw line for a two-shot or three-shot foul sequence. (Visual cue: Shooter spinning the ball or taking deep breaths before the referee hands them the ball; Audio cue: Announcer stating the player's season free-throw percentage.)
editor_action: Frame the shooter from the chest or waist up on CAM-3 (Player Close-Up) during their pre-shot breathing routine, then cut to the wide sideline view (CAM-1, Main Wide) before they bend their knees to shoot so the ball's arc and rebounders are fully visible (example: cut to wide ~1.0s before release). Recommended framing: Tight Hero Close-Up (CAM-3, Player Close-Up) -> Main Sideline (CAM-1, Main Wide).
timing_constraint: Target window: cut to wide ~1.0s before release. Never stay on a tight face close-up while the free throw is actually in the air.
plain_english_tip: Offensive Rebound: Catching your own team's missed shot resets the NCAA shot clock to 20 seconds for an extra scoring chance.

title: Inbound Passer Plus Five Cutters Framing Under Basket
trigger_condition: An offensive team is inbounding the ball from directly underneath their own basket (baseline out of bounds) with less than 20 seconds on the shot clock. (Visual cue: One player holding the ball out of bounds under the hoop while four teammates stack or screen in the paint; Audio cue: Referee hands the ball to the baseline inbounder.)
editor_action: Frame CAM-1 (Main Wide) so the baseline inbounder, the four cutting teammates in the half-court, and the basket are all clearly inside the frame before the referee hands the ball over (example: baseline-inclusive half-court framing). Recommended framing: Main Sideline Camera (CAM-1, Main Wide).
timing_constraint: Do not stay on a tight close-up of the inbounder's face once the referee hands them the ball, because baseline inbound plays often result in an instant layup within 1 second.
plain_english_tip: The Paint: The rectangular lane under the hoop where inside scorers battle (offensive players cannot camp inside it for >3 seconds).

title: Referee Hand-Signal Screen-Side Continuity
trigger_condition: A referee blows the whistle for a blocking vs. charging call and runs toward the scorer's table to give the signal. (Visual cue: Referee moving laterally across the court to face the television cameras; Audio cue: Whistle and crowd anticipation for the call.)
editor_action: Ensure the camera showing the referee's signal is positioned on the same side of the court as CAM-1 (Main Wide) so the referee's pointing arm points toward the actual basket of the team awarded the ball on the television screen (example: left-pointing signal means ball goes to the left-side basket). Recommended framing: Main Sideline (CAM-1, Main Wide) -> Referee Iso (CAM-3, Player Close-Up).
timing_constraint: Never show a referee pointing direction from a reverse far-side camera, which would make the pointing direction appear backwards to the viewer (Enforce >= 1.5s shot-hold minimum and preserve 180-degree court direction across cuts.)
plain_english_tip: Charge vs. Block: Running into a stationary defender outside the small hoop arc is an offensive turnover ('charge').

title: Long Outlet Pass Pan Continuity (No Mid-Flight Cuts)
trigger_condition: After grabbing a defensive rebound, a player hurls a 60-foot baseball pass down the court to a sprinting teammate. (Visual cue: The basketball flying in a long arc across the midcourt line; Audio cue: Crowd gasps as the long pass travels downcourt.)
editor_action: Pan continuously with the flight of the ball on CAM-1 (Main Wide) from the rebounder's hands all the way to the receiver's catch and layup, never cutting mid-flight (example: continuous ~2.5s full-court pan). Recommended framing: Main Sideline Camera (CAM-1, Main Wide).
timing_constraint: Zoom out slightly during the pan so both the flying ball and the sprinting target player come into view before the catch.
plain_english_tip: 10-Second Backcourt: The offense has 10 seconds to dribble across the center line and cannot pass back behind it once across.

title: Pick-And-Roll Two-Man Action Wide Hold on CAM-1
trigger_condition: An offensive teammate sets a screen ('pick') for the ball-handler near the top of the 3-point arc and rolls toward the basket.
editor_action: Never cut to a tight isolation camera during a pick-and-roll. Stay on CAM-1 (Main Wide) so viewers can see whether the ball-handler shoots, drives, or passes to the rolling teammate or an open corner shooter.
timing_constraint: Hold CAM-1 Wide through the entire screen, roll, and pass/shot decision.
plain_english_tip: Screen (Pick): An offensive teammate stands still to block a defender and create open space, then cuts ('rolls') toward the hoop.

title: Star Player Close-Up Budget (Highlighting Key Scorers Without Losing The Game)
trigger_condition: Macro Game Pattern (Full-Game Close-Up Allocation): Using CAM-3 (the tight single-player camera) across a full broadcast to introduce and follow the star players.
editor_action: Give CAM-3 (Player Close-Up) roughly 12% to 15% of total broadcast air time (about one-quarter of all non-wide cuts), saving it for moments RIGHT AFTER a basket is made, while a player walks to the free-throw line, or after a big defensive stop so viewers learn the faces and emotions of the main players without ever missing live passing or shooting.
timing_constraint: Hold player close-ups briefly during normal play and cut them short whenever the other team rushes the ball back up the court (example: 1.5s to 2.8s normal hold, or sub-second 0.7s on a fast break).
plain_english_tip: Fast Break & Press: Sprinting to score before defenders set up, or guarding full-court immediately after a made basket.

title: Final Horn Closure: Winning Celebration, Coach Handshake Line & Arena Scene
trigger_condition: Macro Game Pattern (Post-Game Final Buzzer Arc): The game clock hits 00:00.0 at the end of the game.
editor_action: Give the viewer a complete emotional ending in three smooth shots: (1) hold CAM-1 (Main Wide) Wide through the final horn so viewers see the whole court as the game ends, (2) cut to CAM-3 (Player Close-Up) close-ups of the winning players celebrating, and (3) cut to CAM-4 (Coach & Bench) showing the two head coaches shaking hands at mid-court while the 'FINAL' score banner locks in at the bottom of the screen.
timing_constraint: Sequence wide buzzer -> player celebration -> coach handshake across the post-game window (example: 12s to 18s closing sequence).
plain_english_tip: 10-Second Backcourt: The offense has 10 seconds to dribble across the center line and cannot pass back behind it once across.

title: 10-Second Backcourt Pressure (Crossing The Mid-Court Line in Time)
trigger_condition: Defenders trap the ball-handler in the back half of the court right after an inbound pass.
editor_action: In college basketball, the team with the ball has 10 seconds (until the 30-second shot timer reaches 20) to dribble or pass the ball across the mid-court line. Keep CAM-1 (Main Wide) Wide framed so both the trapped ball-handler and the mid-court line are visible at all times.
timing_constraint: Hold CAM-1 Wide continuously from the inbound pass until the ball crosses the mid-court line or a 10-second violation whistle blows.
plain_english_tip: 10-Second Backcourt: The offense has 10 seconds to dribble across the center line and cannot pass back behind it once across.

title: Fast-Break 'Lead Room' Framing on CAM-1 (Showing The Court Ahead of The Ball)
trigger_condition: A team grabs a rebound or steal and sprints downcourt on a fast break on CAM-1 (Main Wide).
editor_action: Pan CAM-1 (Main Wide) slightly ahead of the player dribbling the ball so roughly two-thirds of the television screen shows the open court, passing lanes, and defenders in front of the ball rather than empty floor behind them.
timing_constraint: Maintain forward lead room (~65% of horizontal frame ahead of the ball-handler) throughout transition sprints.
plain_english_tip: Fast Break & Press: Sprinting to score before defenders set up, or guarding full-court immediately after a made basket.

title: Half-Court Zoom-Corridor Adaptation (Keeping All 10 Players & Both Corners Visible)
trigger_condition: A team slows down and sets up its normal half-court offense on CAM-1 (Main Wide).
editor_action: Keep CAM-1 (Main Wide) zoomed wide enough to show from the top of the 3-point arc all the way to both baseline corners so viewers can see off-ball screens and open 3-point shooters waiting in the corners. Tighten slightly only when the ball is passed inside near the basket.
timing_constraint: Maintain full half-court 10-player framing during perimeter ball movement; allow modest zoom-in only on low-post entries (Maintain steady framing for >= 1.5s hold floor and return to CAM-1 before live shot release.)
plain_english_tip: Screen (Pick): An offensive teammate stands still to block a defender and create open space, then cuts ('rolls') toward the hoop.

title: Minimum Shot-Hold Floor (Preventing Rapid 'Ping-Pong' Camera Flicker)
trigger_condition: Several events happen back-to-back within a second or two (such as a blocked shot, a scramble for the ball, and a quick foul whistle).
editor_action: Never bounce rapidly between three different cameras in under two seconds ('ping-pong cutting'), which disorients viewers. Enforce a minimum hold floor on any live camera cut unless an emergency fast-break bailout back to CAM-1 (Main Wide) Wide is required.
timing_constraint: Maintain a minimum camera hold floor between normal cuts so the broadcast never flickers (example: 1.2s to 1.5s minimum dwell floor).
plain_english_tip: Fast Break & Press: Sprinting to score before defenders set up, or guarding full-court immediately after a made basket.

title: Net-Splash 'Eye-Trace' Beat Before Cutting to The Shooter Close-Up
trigger_condition: A player shoots a jump shot or 3-pointer on CAM-1 (Main Wide) and the ball goes through the hoop.
editor_action: When a shot is in the air, the viewer's eyes are fixed on the basket rim. Wait a brief beat after the ball splashes cleanly through the net before cutting to CAM-3 (Player Close-Up) so the viewer's brain registers that the shot went in before the camera switches to the player's face.
timing_constraint: Hold CAM-1 for a brief beat after the ball clears the net before cutting to CAM-3 (example: 0.3s to 0.5s post-splash eye-trace beat).
plain_english_tip: 3-Pointer: Any shot released from behind the large painted arc counts for 3 points instead of 2.

title: Free-Throw Clutch Pressure Framing in The Final 2 Minutes
trigger_condition: Macro game pattern when a player shoots free throws in the final 2 minutes with the score within 3 points.
editor_action: Hold a tight, steady CAM-3 (Player Close-Up) close-up on the shooter's eyes and deep breath for 3 seconds before the referee hands them the ball, then cut to CAM-1 (Main Wide) for the actual release.
timing_constraint: 3.0s pre-release pressure close-up on CAM-3 before cutting to CAM-1 for the shot.
plain_english_tip: Free Throw: An unguarded 1-point penalty shot from 15 feet while the game clock is stopped.

title: Airball or Badly Missed Shot: Hold CAM-1 for Live Rebound & Runout
trigger_condition: A shooter launches a 3-pointer or jumper that misses the rim completely ('airball').
editor_action: Because airballs often fall straight into a defender's hands for an immediate fast break, stay locked on CAM-1 (Main Wide) Wide and do not cut to a close-up of the shooter.
timing_constraint: Maintain continuous CAM-1 Wide coverage through the rebound and transition (Execute within <= 1.0s reaction window and return to CAM-1 before live ball.)
plain_english_tip: Fast Break & Press: Sprinting to score before defenders set up, or guarding full-court immediately after a made basket.

title: Coach Calling Play Signals from The Sideline on Slow Walk-Ups
trigger_condition: A point guard slowly dribbles up the court while looking over at their head coach holding up hand signals.
editor_action: Keep CAM-1 (Main Wide) framed so the near sideline is visible (or use a brief 1.5s dead-ball CAM-4 (Coach & Bench) cut before the inbound) rather than cutting away from CAM-1 (Main Wide) after the guard crosses mid-court.
timing_constraint: Never cut away to CAM-4 once the ball-handler has crossed the mid-court line in live play (Execute within <= 1.0s reaction window and return to CAM-1 before live ball.)
plain_english_tip: 10-Second Backcourt: The offense has 10 seconds to dribble across the center line and cannot pass back behind it once across.

title: 4-Point Play (Made 3-Pointer Plus Foul) Reaction Sequence
trigger_condition: A shooter drains a 3-pointer while being knocked down by a defender, and the referee signals the basket counts plus 1 free throw.
editor_action: Punch immediately to CAM-3 (Player Close-Up)/CAM-2 (Baseline Low) as teammates help the shooter off the floor and celebrate the rare 4-point play opportunity, holding for 3.0s to 4.0s before rolling the slow-motion replay.
timing_constraint: Extended 3.0s to 4.0s hero celebration hold during the dead-ball foul stoppage.
plain_english_tip: And-One: If a player scores while being fouled, the basket counts and they earn 1 bonus free throw.

title: 2-On-1 or 3-On-1 Fast-Break Lob Anticipation
trigger_condition: Two or three offensive players sprint ahead of a single lone defender on a fast break.
editor_action: Keep CAM-1 (Main Wide) framed slightly wider vertically near the rim to anticipate a high alley-oop lob pass so the ball never rises above the top edge of the television frame.
timing_constraint: Add upper vertical headroom on CAM-1 during multi-player fast breaks (Execute within <= 1.0s reaction window and return to CAM-1 before live ball.)
plain_english_tip: Fast Break & Press: Sprinting to score before defenders set up, or guarding full-court immediately after a made basket.

title: Framing Free Throws: Close-Up Before The Shot, Wide View on The Final Shot for The Rebound
trigger_condition: A fouled player is taking one, two, or three unguarded free-throw shots from the free-throw line.
editor_action: While the player bounces the ball and prepares to shoot, frame them up close on CAM-3 (Player Close-Up) so viewers can see their focus. Before the final free throw is released (when the ball will stay live if it misses), switch back to CAM-1 (Main Wide) so viewers can see the tall players battling for the rebound around the basket.
timing_constraint: Close-up on CAM-3 during the pre-shot routine, switching to CAM-1 Wide before the final live free throw leaves the shooter's hands.
plain_english_tip: Offensive Rebound: Catching your own team's missed shot resets the NCAA shot clock to 20 seconds for an extra scoring chance.

title: Showing All 10 Players on Out-Of-Bounds Throw-Ins Under The Basket
trigger_condition: The ball went out of bounds near the basket ('baseline') or along the side ('sideline'), and an offensive player has 5 seconds to pass it back into play.
editor_action: Return to CAM-1 (Main Wide) before the referee hands the ball to the passer. Teams often run quick, rehearsed plays on throw-ins to get an instant layup or 3-pointer, and only the wide camera shows the screens and cuts happening away from the ball.
timing_constraint: Cut to CAM-1 Wide at least a full second before the referee hands the ball to the inbound passer (example: 1.0s to 1.5s pre-inbound wide setup).
plain_english_tip: 3-Pointer: Any shot released from behind the large painted arc counts for 3 points instead of 2.

title: The 'And-One' 3-Point / 4-Point Play Sequence (Basket Counts Plus a Bonus Foul Shot)
trigger_condition: A shooter is fouled by a defender in the act of shooting, and the ball STILL goes into the basket ('an and-one').
editor_action: When a player scores while being fouled, the basket counts AND they earn one bonus free throw. Hold CAM-1 (Main Wide) until the ball drops through the net, then immediately punch to CAM-3 (Hero Player Iso) to show both the referee signaling that the basket counts and the player celebrating before they walk to the free-throw line.
timing_constraint: Hold wide until the ball clears the net, then cut to CAM-3 for the celebration and referee 'basket counts' signal (example: 2.5s to 3.2s hold).
plain_english_tip: Bonus rule: At 7+ team fouls in a half, opponents shoot 1-and-1 free throws; at 10+ fouls (Double Bonus), they get 2 automatic free throws.

title: Explaining Intentional Late-Game Fouls (Fouling on Purpose to Stop The Clock)
trigger_condition: In the final minute of a close game, the trailing team intentionally wraps up or taps the ball-handler right after the throw-in to stop the game clock.
editor_action: Newcomers often wonder why a defender fouls on purpose late in the game: stay on CAM-1 (Main Wide) Wide during the throw-in so viewers see the trailing defense trying to steal the pass first and then intentionally fouling to stop the clock and force free throws, followed by a quick CAM-4 (Coach & Bench) glimpse of the coach confirming the strategy.
timing_constraint: Keep CAM-1 Wide through the throw-in and intentional foul whistle, then cut briefly to the sideline coach (example: 2.0s coach cut).
plain_english_tip: Free Throw: An unguarded 1-point penalty shot from 15 feet while the game clock is stopped.

title: Headroom & Face Visibility Verification on Player Close-Ups (CAM-3)
trigger_condition: CAM-3 (Player Close-Up) is candidate-scored before putting it on air after a basket or foul whistle.
editor_action: Verify that the player's face and jersey number are clearly centered in the frame with proper headroom above their head (and not cut off at the chin or blocked by another player walking past) before switching to CAM-3 (Player Close-Up).
timing_constraint: Verify clean face/torso framing in the 0.3s pre-cut window before taking CAM-3 to Program.

title: Low-Post Back-Down & Double-Team Kickout Wide Framing
trigger_condition: A tall center catches the ball with their back to the basket near the painted lane and defenders collapse to double-team them.
editor_action: Stay on CAM-1 (Main Wide) rather than punching to CAM-2 (Baseline Low) Baseline during the dribble back-down because post double-teams frequently result in a cross-court 'kickout' pass to an open 3-point shooter.
timing_constraint: Hold CAM-1 until the post player actually rises for a layup/dunk or completes the kickout pass.
plain_english_tip: The Paint: The rectangular lane under the hoop where inside scorers battle (offensive players cannot camp inside it for >3 seconds).

title: Charge Taken: Defender on The Floor + Bench Celebration Cut
trigger_condition: A defender plants their feet outside the restricted arc, absorbs a collision, and the referee signals an offensive charging foul.
editor_action: Cut to CAM-2 (Baseline Low) or CAM-3 (Player Close-Up) showing teammates rushing over to pull the defender up off the floor, followed by a brief cut to their cheering bench on CAM-4 (Coach & Bench).
timing_constraint: Show teammate help-up and bench reaction during the turnover handoff (example: 3.5s total).
plain_english_tip: Charge vs. Block: Running into a stationary defender outside the small hoop arc is an offensive turnover ('charge').

title: Following The 'Hot Hand' (When One Player Cannot Miss)
trigger_condition: Macro Game Pattern (Multi-Possession Scoring Streak): A single player makes three or more shots in a row and becomes the main story of the half.
editor_action: Treat the hot scorer as the main character of the current chapter: after they score, hold their close-up slightly longer, show the defenders trying to guard them more tightly during dead-ball pauses, and update their point total on screen after each make so viewers can follow their streak.
timing_constraint: Check in on the hot scorer with a brief close-up + updated scoring stat during dead balls across their streak (example: every 2 to 3 possessions while hot).

title: Commentator 'Look-At' Visual Follow (Matching Camera Cuts to What Announcers Say)
trigger_condition: During a dead ball, free-throw walk-up, or slow half-court walk-up, the commentator explicitly calls out a specific player, coach, or bench reaction (such as 'Look at how tired he looks' or 'Watch the coach on the sideline right now').
editor_action: When the announcer points out a specific person or reaction, the viewer naturally wants to see it. Cut to the matching isolation camera (CAM-3 (Player Close-Up) Player Close-Up or CAM-4 (Coach & Bench) Coach/Bench) within a brief beat so the picture proves what the announcer is describing, then return to CAM-1 (Main Wide) Wide before live ball movement speeds up.
timing_constraint: Switch within a brief beat of the spoken cue and hold while the commentator finishes the point (example: 1.0s audio-to-cut lag, 3.0s to 4.5s visual hold).
plain_english_tip: Free Throw: An unguarded 1-point penalty shot from 15 feet while the game clock is stopped.

title: Player Technical or Flagrant Ejection Walk-Off Follow
trigger_condition: A player or coach is ejected from the game (two technical fouls or a Flagrant 2 foul) and must walk to the locker room tunnel.
editor_action: Follow the ejected player or coach on CAM-3 (Player Close-Up)/CAM-4 (Coach & Bench) as they walk toward the arena tunnel during the extended stoppage before transitioning back to CAM-1 (Main Wide) for the free throws.
timing_constraint: Follow tunnel walk-off during the dead-ball stoppage (example: 6.0s to 8.0s).
plain_english_tip: Free Throw: An unguarded 1-point penalty shot from 15 feet while the game clock is stopped.

title: Buzzer-Horn Audio Priority at Half or Shot-Clock Expiration
trigger_condition: The game clock or 30-second shot clock reaches 0.0 and the arena horn sounds. (Visual cue: Red or amber LED light strips illuminating around the backboard and shot clock; Audio cue: The loud arena horn or buzzer signaling time expiration.)
editor_action: Ensure the arena horn is clearly audible in the broadcast mix so the viewer immediately knows whether a shot was released before time expired, and sync any replay cut to the exact start of the horn (example: horn onset aligned within ~50ms of LED illumination). Recommended framing: Main Sideline Camera (CAM-1, Main Wide) or Backboard Replay.
timing_constraint: Target window: horn onset aligned within ~50ms of LED illumination. Do not let music stingers or transition sound effects drown out the official game horn.
plain_english_tip: Two Clocks: Teams have 30 seconds on the shot clock to hit the rim on each possession while the 20-minute half clock counts down.

title: Corner Three-Pointer Edge-Of-Frame Buffer
trigger_condition: An offensive shooter spots up in the deep near-side or far-side corner of the court near the sideline. (Visual cue: A wing player standing within two feet of the corner out-of-bounds line waiting for a pass; Audio cue: Ball-handler driving into the paint with a corner shooter open.)
editor_action: Ensure the main sideline camera leaves a generous visual margin behind the baseline and corner three-point line so the corner shooter's feet are never cropped off the edge of the screen (example: maintain at least ~5% frame buffer outside the baseline). Recommended framing: Main Sideline Camera (CAM-1, Main Wide).
timing_constraint: Target window: maintain at least ~5% frame buffer outside the baseline. Never zoom in so tightly on the ball-handler in the paint that an open corner shooter disappears off the bottom or side edge of the television frame.
plain_english_tip: The Paint: The rectangular lane under the hoop where inside scorers battle (offensive players cannot camp inside it for >3 seconds).

title: Jib / Crane Sweep over Crowd Only During Stoppages
trigger_condition: The robotic crane (jib) camera behind the basket sweeps high over the cheering baseline crowd. (Visual cue: Sweeping cinematic motion rising from floor level toward the upper bowl; Audio cue: Timeout horn and upbeat arena music.)
editor_action: Use sweeping crane or jib camera movements exclusively when the game clock is stopped (timeouts, media timeout breaks, pre-game introductions) to create a grand arena atmosphere without risking disorientation during live play (example: ~3.5s crane sweep going to commercial). Recommended framing: Baseline Crane / Jib (CAM-5, Above-Rim).
timing_constraint: Target window: ~3.5s crane sweep going to commercial. Never cut to a moving crane shot while the basketball is live in play.
plain_english_tip: Two Clocks: Teams have 30 seconds on the shot clock to hit the rim on each possession while the 20-minute half clock counts down.

title: Consistent Left-To-Right / Right-To-Left Offensive Direction Reminder
trigger_condition: At the start of the second half (after halftime), the two teams switch which basket they are attacking. (Visual cue: First offensive possession of the second half; Audio cue: Play-by-play welcomes viewers back to the start of the second half.)
editor_action: Hold on the wide sideline camera for the entire opening possession of the second half so casual viewers immediately adjust to the fact that each team is now shooting at the opposite end of the screen (example: uninterrupted ~15-24s opening second-half wide shot). Recommended framing: Main Sideline Camera (CAM-1, Main Wide).
timing_constraint: Do not use reverse-angle or baseline cuts during the first possession after halftime.

title: Post-Score Jog-Back Direction Match
trigger_condition: After scoring a basket on the right-hand hoop, the scorer jogs back toward the left-hand side of the court on defense. (Visual cue: Player backpedaling or jogging from right to left across the floor; Audio cue: Crowd cheering and announcer calling the basket.)
editor_action: When cutting from CAM-1 (Main Wide) to CAM-3 (Player Close-Up) and back to CAM-1 (Main Wide), ensure the player is moving in the exact same screen direction (right-to-left or left-to-right) in all three shots so the motion flows seamlessly across every cut (example: consistent right-to-left motion vector across all sideline cameras). Recommended framing: Main Sideline (CAM-1, Main Wide) -> Hero Iso (CAM-3, Player Close-Up) -> Main Sideline (CAM-1, Main Wide).
timing_constraint: Do not cut to a reverse-side camera during the jog-back, which would make the player appear to suddenly run toward the wrong basket (Enforce >= 1.5s shot-hold minimum and preserve 180-degree court direction across cuts.)

title: Tracking a Star Player Sitting on The Bench in 'Foul Trouble'
trigger_condition: Macro Game Pattern (Star Player Sidelined by Fouls): A team's best player has to sit on the bench for a long stretch because they are close to the 5-foul disqualification limit.
editor_action: Help viewers understand why the star is missing from the court: periodically cut to CAM-4 (the bench camera) during dead-ball whistles to show the sidelined star watching from the bench alongside a simple note showing how many fouls they have and how the score has changed since they sat down.
timing_constraint: Brief bench check-in during dead-ball pauses while the star is sidelined so viewers remember why they are out (example: once every 4 to 6 minutes of game clock).
plain_english_tip: Foul Limit: In college basketball, any player who commits 5 personal fouls is disqualified for the rest of the game.

title: Sideline Reporter Hand-Off Audio Pre-Clearance
trigger_condition: The play-by-play announcer tosses the broadcast to the courtside reporter for an injury or coaching update. (Visual cue: Play-by-play says 'Let's send it down to courtside...' during a dead ball or free-throw setup; Audio cue: Sideline reporter's directional headset microphone channel opening.)
editor_action: Open the sideline reporter's audio channel a fraction of a second before cutting to their camera and compress surrounding crowd noise so their voice is immediately clear from the first word (example: 200ms audio pre-open before video cut). Recommended framing: Sideline Reporter Medium (CAM-4, Coach & Bench).
timing_constraint: If live play resumes while the reporter is still speaking, switch the video back to CAM-1 (Main Wide) while keeping the reporter's audio open in a split-screen or voiceover until they finish their sentence.
plain_english_tip: Free Throw: An unguarded 1-point penalty shot from 15 feet while the game clock is stopped.

title: Promo Read Voiceover Sync with Full-Screen Schedule Card
trigger_condition: During a second-half timeout return, the play-by-play announcer reads a promotion for an upcoming broadcast on the network. (Visual cue: A full-screen or side-panel graphic showing upcoming team logos, broadcast date, and tip-off time; Audio cue: Announcer reading the scheduled matchup and network time slot.)
editor_action: Display the upcoming schedule graphic in exact synchronization with the announcer's promo read, and dismiss the graphic the instant they finish reading the time slot (example: ~6s promo card duration). Recommended framing: Graphic Overlay over CAM-1 (Main Wide).
timing_constraint: Target window: ~6s promo card duration. Abort the promo graphic immediately if the referee hands the ball to the inbounder to resume live play.

title: Technical Foul Whistle & Crowd Gasp Hold
trigger_condition: A referee blows a sharp whistle and forms a 'T' with their hands to assess a technical foul on a complaining player or coach. (Visual cue: Referee making the unmistakable 'T' hand signal toward the bench or player; Audio cue: Sharp whistle followed by an audible crowd gasp or roar.)
editor_action: Show the referee forming the 'T' signal first so the viewer sees the official penalty, then cut immediately to the player or coach who received the technical while the announcer explains why it was called (example: ~1.5s on referee signal -> ~3.5s on player/coach reaction). Recommended framing: Referee Medium (CAM-3, Player Close-Up) -> Offending Player/Coach (CAM-4, Coach & Bench).
timing_constraint: Target window: ~1.5s on referee signal -> ~3.5s on player/coach reaction. Mute courtside parabolic mics during the argument to prevent broadcasting profanity that triggered the technical foul.

title: Pick-And-Roll Two-Man Framing Balance
trigger_condition: A teammate runs up to set a screen (pick) for the player dribbling the ball near the top of the three-point arc. (Visual cue: Screener planting his feet next to the ball-handler's defender; Audio cue: Commentator calls out the high screen or pick-and-roll action.)
editor_action: Frame the camera wide enough to show the ball-handler, the screener rolling toward the basket, and the help defender near the rim simultaneously so the viewer understands all options of the play (example: full half-court framing from top of key to baseline). Recommended framing: Main Sideline Camera (CAM-1, Main Wide).
timing_constraint: Do not pan strictly with the ball-handler if he dribbles laterally; keep the rolling big man and the basket anchored in the frame (Maintain steady framing for >= 1.5s hold floor and return to CAM-1 before live shot release.)
plain_english_tip: Screen (Pick): An offensive teammate stands still to block a defender and create open space, then cuts ('rolls') toward the hoop.

title: Backcourt Press Wide Zoom-Out
trigger_condition: The defending team applies a full-court man-to-man or zone trap right after a made basket or dead-ball inbound. (Visual cue: Two or more defenders pressuring the inbounder and ball-handler in the backcourt; Audio cue: Commentator calls out 'Full-court pressure here!'.)
editor_action: Zoom CAM-1 (Main Wide) out to its widest comfortable focal length so the viewer can see both the trapped ball-handler in the backcourt and the open passing lanes near midcourt (example: ~70 feet of court length visible in frame). Recommended framing: Main Sideline Camera (CAM-1, Main Wide).
timing_constraint: Smoothly tighten back to standard half-court framing once the ball-handler safely crosses the midcourt timeline (Maintain steady framing for >= 1.5s hold floor and return to CAM-1 before live shot release.)
plain_english_tip: 10-Second Backcourt: The offense has 10 seconds to dribble across the center line and cannot pass back behind it once across.

title: Foot-On-The-Line Zoom Replay for Two vs. Three Point Calls
trigger_condition: A player hits a jump shot with their toes very close to the three-point line, and the referees signal a two-pointer or review the call. (Visual cue: Referee holding up two fingers or rotating their finger for an instant replay check; Audio cue: Commentator wonders 'Did he have a toe on the line?'.)
editor_action: Roll a tight, zoomed-in replay focused specifically on the shooter's sneakers and the painted three-point arc at the moment of release so the viewer can judge for themselves whether it is worth 2 or 3 points (example: 2x digital crop pause on foot release). Recommended framing: Sideline Low-Angle Replay (CAM-2 (Baseline Low) or CAM-3 (Player Close-Up)).
timing_constraint: Keep the replay brief (~3-4 seconds) if play is continuing live, or hold longer during an official stoppage.
plain_english_tip: 3-Pointer: Any shot released from behind the large painted arc counts for 3 points instead of 2.

title: Jump-Cut Prevention Between Similar Focal Lengths
trigger_condition: Two different cameras are both framed on the same star player from nearly the same angle and distance. (Visual cue: Two sideline cameras both holding medium waist-up shots of the same player; Audio cue: Dead-ball commentary.)
editor_action: Never cut directly from one camera to another if both cameras have nearly the same angle (< 30 degrees separation) and focal size on the same player, as this creates a jarring 'jump cut' where the player appears to twitch in place (example: require >= 30 degree angle change or distinct shot size change from wide to tight). Recommended framing: Tight Hero Close-Up (CAM-3, Player Close-Up).
timing_constraint: Stay on the current camera rather than switching to a nearly identical neighboring camera (Enforce >= 1.5s shot-hold minimum and preserve 180-degree court direction across cuts.)

title: Rim-Mic Impact Spike During Dunk Hold
trigger_condition: A player slams the ball through the hoop (dunk), causing the rim microphone to register a loud metallic thud. (Visual cue: A player hangs on or releases the rim as the net snaps upward; Audio cue: A sharp, resonant metallic rim-clank and backboard vibration.)
editor_action: Boost the rim-microphone audio channel briefly at the moment of impact and hold the camera cut for a beat so the viewer hears and feels the physical force of the dunk (example: +4 dB rim-mic transient boost for ~0.6s). Recommended framing: Low-Angle Basket Stinger (CAM-5, Above-Rim) or Main Game Camera.
timing_constraint: Target window: +4 dB rim-mic transient boost for ~0.6s. Apply a hard audio limiter so the rim impact never clips or distorts the broadcast master mix.
plain_english_tip: Dunk & Block: Slamming the ball directly through the rim, or leaping to swat an opponent's shot away.

title: Post-Game On-Court Interview Headset Isolation
trigger_condition: Immediately after the final buzzer, the sideline reporter interviews the player of the game on the court while arena music blares. (Visual cue: Player wearing a broadcast headset or speaking into a handheld directional mic near midcourt; Audio cue: High ambient arena PA music and departing crowd chatter.)
editor_action: Route the post-game interview through a tight noise-suppressing vocal chain and lower the arena stereo mics by at least 15 dB so every word of the exhausted player's reflection is effortless to hear (example: -16 dB ambient bed during live interview). Recommended framing: Tight Hero Close-Up (CAM-3, Player Close-Up).
timing_constraint: Target window: -16 dB ambient bed during live interview. Keep a secondary camera framing both the reporter and the player in case a teammate runs into the frame to celebrate or photobomb.
plain_english_tip: 10-Second Backcourt: The offense has 10 seconds to dribble across the center line and cannot pass back behind it once across.

title: Vertical Tilt Headroom on High-Arcing Shots & Alley-Oops
trigger_condition: A player launches a high-arcing rainbow three-pointer or throws a high lob pass toward the rim for an alley-oop dunk. (Visual cue: The basketball rising steeply toward the top edge of the camera frame; Audio cue: Rising crowd anticipation as the lob or deep shot climbs.)
editor_action: Tilt the camera slightly upward or zoom out smoothly as the ball climbs so the basketball never vanishes above the top border of the television screen during its flight (example: keep the apex of the ball's arc inside the top 10% of the frame). Recommended framing: Main Sideline Camera (CAM-1, Main Wide).
timing_constraint: Target window: keep the apex of the ball's arc inside the top 10% of the frame. Keep the players' feet and the floor visible at the bottom of the frame so the viewer does not lose spatial orientation on the court.
plain_english_tip: 3-Pointer: Any shot released from behind the large painted arc counts for 3 points instead of 2.

title: Rim-Level Robotic Camera Framing on Block Replays
trigger_condition: A defender leaps at the rim to block or contest a dunk/layup attempt, and a replay is queued. (Visual cue: Defender's hand meeting the ball right above the cylinder of the rim; Audio cue: Announcer questioning whether the block was clean or a goaltending violation.)
editor_action: Select the backboard or rim-level camera angle for the replay so the viewer can clearly see whether the ball was still rising or touching the backboard when the defender made contact (example: slow-motion 50% speed near the apex). Recommended framing: Above-Rim / Backboard Replay (CAM-5, Above-Rim).
timing_constraint: Target window: slow-motion 50% speed near the apex. Follow with a baseline angle if the rim camera is partially obstructed by the net or the player's shoulders.
plain_english_tip: Goaltending: Defenders cannot swat a shot once it is on its downward arc toward the hoop; doing so awards automatic points.

title: Out-Of-Bounds Deflection Hand-Detail Zoom
trigger_condition: Two players slap at a loose rebound going out of bounds, and officials must decide which hand touched the ball last. (Visual cue: Ball deflecting off fingertips near the baseline or sideline; Audio cue: Commentator says 'Let's see who touched that last.'.)
editor_action: Queue a super-slow-motion replay framed tightly on the players' hands and the basketball so the viewer can see the spin of the ball change as it brushes a fingertip (example: 120fps slow-mo zoomed on hand contact). Recommended framing: High-Frame-Rate Baseline Replay (CAM-2, Baseline Low).
timing_constraint: Pair two angles side-by-side or sequentially if a player's arm blocks the first camera's line of sight (Maintain steady framing for >= 1.5s hold floor and return to CAM-1 before live shot release.)
plain_english_tip: Offensive Rebound: Catching your own team's missed shot resets the NCAA shot clock to 20 seconds for an extra scoring chance.

title: End-Of-Game Handshake Line Medium Tracking
trigger_condition: The final horn sounds and opposing players and coaches meet at midcourt to shake hands and embrace. (Visual cue: Star players from both teams hugging and exchanging words at center court; Audio cue: Commentators wrapping up the game storyline and final statistics.)
editor_action: Follow the star players with smooth medium waist-up shots as they greet opposing stars and coaches, holding for 3 to 5 seconds on meaningful exchanges of sportsmanship (example: ~4s hold on the two leading scorers embracing). Recommended framing: Tight Hero Close-Up (CAM-3, Player Close-Up) & Baseline Handheld (CAM-2, Baseline Low).
timing_constraint: Target window: ~4s hold on the two leading scorers embracing. Keep the camera movement calm and steady rather than whip-panning between random players in the crowd.
plain_english_tip: 10-Second Backcourt: The offense has 10 seconds to dribble across the center line and cannot pass back behind it once across.

title: Passer-To-Scorer Two-Shot Bridging Before Single Iso
trigger_condition: A point guard delivers a brilliant no-look or cross-court assist to a teammate for a layup or dunk. (Visual cue: Scorer points back at the passer in appreciation as both jog up the court; Audio cue: Commentator praises the vision of the passer.)
editor_action: Wait on the wide angle for a brief beat as the scorer points to the passer so the viewer sees the spatial connection between the two teammates before cutting to a single close-up of either player (example: ~1.0s wide connection hold before iso cut). Recommended framing: Main Sideline (CAM-1, Main Wide) -> Hero Iso (CAM-3, Player Close-Up).
timing_constraint: Target window: ~1.0s wide connection hold before iso cut. If cutting between separate close-ups of the scorer and passer, ensure their eyelines face toward each other across the cut (e.g., scorer looking right, passer looking left).
plain_english_tip: Dunk & Block: Slamming the ball directly through the rim, or leaping to swat an opponent's shot away.

title: Split-Screen Spatial Alignment (Live Left/right vs. Isolated Subject)
trigger_condition: A double-box split screen is used to show a live inbound or free throw alongside a coach interview or replay. (Visual cue: Two side-by-side video boxes on the broadcast screen; Audio cue: Sideline reporter or analyst speaking while live setup occurs.)
editor_action: Place the live game feed (CAM-1, Main Wide) in the larger primary box on the left and the secondary subject on the right, and animate the primary box smoothly to full-screen when live play accelerates so the viewer's eyes never lose the live court (example: 65%/35% box ratio expanding over ~0.4s). Recommended framing: Double-Box Split (CAM-1 (Main Wide) + CAM-4 (Coach & Bench)).
timing_constraint: Target window: 65%/35% box ratio expanding over ~0.4s. Never instantaneously pop the live court box from one side of the screen to the other.
plain_english_tip: Free Throw: An unguarded 1-point penalty shot from 15 feet while the game clock is stopped.

title: Avoiding 'Jump Cuts' Between Two Similar Wide Camera Angles
trigger_condition: Switching from CAM-1 (Main Wide) to another camera angle.
editor_action: Always cut between clearly different zoom levels or perspectives (such as Wide CAM-1 (Main Wide) to Close-Up CAM-3 (Player Close-Up) or Low Baseline CAM-2 (Baseline Low)). Never cut from one wide mid-court camera to another wide mid-court camera with nearly the same view, which looks like a jarring visual glitch ('jump cut').
timing_constraint: Require a clear change in focal length (wide vs. tight) or camera elevation (high vs. baseline) on every cut.
plain_english_tip: 10-Second Backcourt: The offense has 10 seconds to dribble across the center line and cannot pass back behind it once across.

title: Blocked Shot into Out-Of-Bounds Blocker Reaction Cut
trigger_condition: A defender swats a layup or jump shot out of bounds, stopping the game clock.
editor_action: Immediately cut to CAM-2 (Baseline Low) or CAM-3 (Defender Close-Up) showing the shot-blocker's reaction for 2.0s to 3.0s while the referee retrieves the ball for the throw-in.
timing_constraint: Hold blocker reaction during the dead-ball retrieval window (example: 2.5s cut).
plain_english_tip: Dunk & Block: Slamming the ball directly through the rim, or leaping to swat an opponent's shot away.

title: Scorer's Table Substitution Waiting Area Check
trigger_condition: Two or three backup players kneel at the scorer's table waiting for the next whistle to enter the game.
editor_action: Only show players waiting at the scorer's table during a dead-ball pause or free-throw walk-up on CAM-4 (Coach & Bench); never cut away from live half-court action to show the scorer's table.
timing_constraint: Dead-ball only CAM-4 check-in (example: 2.0s to 3.0s during substitution horn).
plain_english_tip: Free Throw: An unguarded 1-point penalty shot from 15 feet while the game clock is stopped.

title: Between-Free-Throws High-Five & Shooter Routine Framing
trigger_condition: A player finishes the 1st free throw of a 2-shot trip and teammates step in to slap hands before the 2nd shot.
editor_action: Cut to CAM-2 (Baseline Low) or CAM-3 (Player Close-Up) for a 2.5s medium close-up of the shooter's between-shot routine and high-fives, then return to CAM-1 (Main Wide) before the referee bounces the ball for the 2nd shot.
timing_constraint: Hold CAM-2/CAM-3 for ~2.5s between Shot 1 and Shot 2; return to CAM-1 before ball bounce.
plain_english_tip: Free Throw: An unguarded 1-point penalty shot from 15 feet while the game clock is stopped.

title: Step-Back 3-Pointer Ankle-Breaker Reaction
trigger_condition: A ball-handler uses a sharp dribble move to make the defender stumble, steps back behind the arc, and hits a 3-pointer.
editor_action: After the net splash on CAM-1, cut to CAM-3 (Player Close-Up) on the shooter for 2.0s while the Replay Agent immediately clips the dribble separation for the next whistle pause.
timing_constraint: 2.0s CAM-3 celebration cut on normal walk-ups; clip separation move for next stoppage.
plain_english_tip: 3-Pointer: Any shot released from behind the large painted arc counts for 3 points instead of 2.

title: Victory Dribble-Out (Final 10 Seconds When Trailing Team Stops Fouling)
trigger_condition: In the final 10 seconds of the game, the leading team holds a safe lead, the trailing defense stands back and stops fouling, and the point guard dribbles out the clock.
editor_action: Hold a wide CAM-1 (Main Wide) view for the first few seconds of the dribble-out, then cut to CAM-4 (Coach & Bench) on the winning head coach and bench celebrating as the final 3 seconds tick down to 00:00.
timing_constraint: Hold CAM-1 until ~03.0s remaining, then cut to winning bench/coach celebration.

title: Following Players Toward Their Bench Huddle When a Timeout Is Called
trigger_condition: A coach or player calls a timeout to stop play and talk strategy with their teammates.
editor_action: Show the player or coach signaling the 'T' timeout sign with their hands, then cut to CAM-4 (Sideline/Bench camera) as the five players on the court walk over to high-five their teammates and gather around their coach's whiteboard.
timing_constraint: Hold the bench huddle walk-up briefly before handing off to the timeout highlight reel or commercial break (example: 3.0s to 4.5s huddle entry).

title: Smooth Post-Free-Throw Zoom-Out into Live Transition
trigger_condition: A player releases the final free throw while CAM-1 (Main Wide) is framed medium-tight on the free-throw lane.
editor_action: As the final free-throw shot is in the air, smoothly zoom CAM-1 (Main Wide) back out to full half-court width so whether the shot goes in or bounces off the rim for a rebound, the transition into live play feels seamless without needing an abrupt jump cut.
timing_constraint: Begin smooth zoom-out on ball release so full-court width is reached as the rebound is secured (example: 1.0s smooth zoom-out).
plain_english_tip: Offensive Rebound: Catching your own team's missed shot resets the NCAA shot clock to 20 seconds for an extra scoring chance.

title: High-Frame-Rate Sharpness Selection for Slow-Motion Contact & Boundary Checks
trigger_condition: Multiple replay cameras (REPLAY-A, REPLAY-B, CAM-5) captured a fast block, finger-tip deflection, or foot-on-the-line call.
editor_action: When slowing video down to half or quarter speed, standard cameras can look blurry during fast hand movement. Automatically select the high-speed replay camera with the sharpest, least motion-blurred view of the ball and hands at the exact frame of contact.
timing_constraint: Rank candidate replay feeds by frame sharpness at the contact timestamp before rolling slow motion (example: 50% to 65% playback speed).

title: Conference Rivalry & Trophy Game Pre-Tip Intensity Framing
trigger_condition: Macro game pattern across rivalry and tournament championship broadcasts during the opening 3 minutes.
editor_action: Interleave CAM-4 (Coach & Bench) student-section and bench intensity shots on the first two dead-ball whistles to capture rivalry atmosphere while returning to CAM-1 (Main Wide) Wide before every throw-in.
timing_constraint: 2 rivalry atmosphere cuts in the opening 3 game minutes (example: 3.0s crowd/bench cut).

title: Drought-Breaker Relief Reaction Cut
trigger_condition: Macro game pattern when a team finally makes a basket to end a 3+ minute scoring drought.
editor_action: Punch to CAM-3 (Player Close-Up) on the scorer and briefly check CAM-4 (Coach & Bench) on the head coach's reaction, while clearing the scoring-drought badge from the scoreboard.
timing_constraint: Hold scorer/coach relief cut on walk-up inbounds (example: 2.5s cut).

title: Loose-Ball Dive on The Floor into Timeout or Held-Ball Whistle
trigger_condition: Two or more players dive onto the hardwood floor for a loose ball and a referee blows the whistle for a jump ball or timeout.
editor_action: Hold CAM-1 (Main Wide) during the dive so viewers see who secured the ball, then cut to CAM-2 (Baseline Low)/CAM-3 (Player Close-Up) at floor level after the whistle blows to show the players untangling and the referee's signal.
timing_constraint: Cut to floor-level CAM-2/CAM-3 after the whistle stops play (example: 3.0s hold).

title: Backdoor Cut & Baseline Reverse Layup Framing
trigger_condition: An offensive player fakes stepping out toward the 3-point line, cuts sharply behind the defender ('backdoor cut'), and finishes a reverse layup under the rim.
editor_action: Hold CAM-1 (Main Wide) through the pass and reverse layup finish, then use a brief 1.5s CAM-2 (Baseline Low) baseline low-angle cut on a slow inbound walk-up.
timing_constraint: Hold CAM-1 through the finish; optional 1.5s CAM-2 cut if opponent walks the ball up.
plain_english_tip: 3-Pointer: Any shot released from behind the large painted arc counts for 3 points instead of 2.

title: Coach Arguments with Referee (Keep Both in Frame Without Missing Play)
trigger_condition: A head coach vehemently argues a call with a referee along the sideline during a dead-ball stoppage.
editor_action: Cut to CAM-4 (Coach & Bench) framed medium-wide to capture both the coach and the referee's body language during the stoppage, and cut back to CAM-1 (Main Wide) immediately if play resumes or a technical foul 'T' is signaled.
timing_constraint: Hold CAM-4 during dead-ball discussion (example: 3.5s); return to CAM-1 before throw-in.

title: Off-Ball Foul Away from The Ball: Show Who Fouled Whom
trigger_condition: A whistle blows for a holding or pushing foul away from the basketball while a guard is dribbling at the top of the key.
editor_action: Cut to CAM-2 (Baseline Low) or CAM-3 (Player Close-Up) focused on the two players involved in the off-ball collision and the referee pointing out the offender so viewers understand why the whistle blew.
timing_constraint: Cut to the off-ball foul pair during the 3.0s dead-ball whistle window.

title: Close-Up Under The Basket After a Dunk or Layup
trigger_condition: A player scores right at the hoop with a dunk or a close-range layup through defenders, and the other team is not rushing the ball back up the court.
editor_action: Switch briefly to CAM-2 (the camera sitting underneath the basket) or CAM-3 (the close-up player camera) right after the ball goes through the net to show the excitement and physical effort up close, then return to the wide camera as the other team brings the ball up.
timing_constraint: Brief celebration close-up after the ball clears the net, returning to the wide view before the ball crosses the middle of the court (example: 1.8s under-basket hold).
plain_english_tip: Dunk & Block: Slamming the ball directly through the rim, or leaping to swat an opponent's shot away.

title: Capturing Arena Crowd Energy After Big Plays Without Losing The Ball
trigger_condition: Macro Game Pattern (Home Crowd Roars & Momentum Peaks): A huge dunk, game-tying 3-pointer, or blocked shot sends the arena crowd into a roar.
editor_action: Let the viewer feel the stadium atmosphere by holding the celebration camera (CAM-2 (Baseline Low) under the hoop or CAM-3 (Player Close-Up) on the player with the crowd cheering behind them) for an extra beat when a timeout is called, while immediately snapping back to the wide camera if the game keeps moving.
timing_constraint: Extend celebration framing when a timeout stops the clock (example: 3.0s to 4.5s crowd roar hold), but cut back in under a second if play continues.
plain_english_tip: 3-Pointer: Any shot released from behind the large painted arc counts for 3 points instead of 2.

title: Showing Who Fouled Whom and The Referee's Signal When a Whistle Blows
trigger_condition: A referee blows the whistle for a personal foul (illegal physical contact such as bumping a driver or reaching in).
editor_action: Help the viewer understand what just happened by cutting briefly to the two players involved in the collision on CAM-2 (Baseline Low) or CAM-3, then showing the referee making the hand signal toward the scorer's table so everyone knows which player was charged with the foul.
timing_constraint: Quick reaction cut to the players and referee signal immediately after the whistle before rolling any slow-motion replay (example: 2.0s to 2.5s whistle reaction).
plain_english_tip: Charge vs. Block: Running into a stationary defender outside the small hoop arc is an offensive turnover ('charge').

title: The 'Sixth Man' Spark-Plug Storyline (When a Backup Player Comes off The Bench and Changes The Game)
trigger_condition: Macro Game Pattern (Bench Contribution Arc): A non-starting substitute player ('sixth man') enters the game from the bench and scores multiple baskets or creates consecutive defensive steals.
editor_action: Introduce the backup player as a new catalyst in the game story: pair their made baskets with a CAM-3 (Player Close-Up) close-up and a CAM-4 (Coach & Bench) cut of their teammates jumping up on the bench to celebrate, and cue a 'Bench Points' comparison graphic on the next whistle so viewers understand how the reserve players are swinging the game.
timing_constraint: Weave player close-up + bench celebration + bench-points graphic across the substitute's hot stretch (example: 2 to 3 possessions).

title: Highlighting The Defensive Stopper & Rim Protector (Storytelling Beyond Scoring)
trigger_condition: Macro Game Pattern (Multi-Possession Defensive Dominance): A specific defender repeatedly blocks shots near the basket, forces steals, or holds the other team's best scorer without a basket over a long stretch.
editor_action: Make sure viewers see that defense wins games too: after a blocked shot, steal, or forced shot-clock violation, give the defensive stopper the CAM-3 (Player Close-Up) hero close-up (normally reserved for scorers) and pair it with a stat banner showing their blocks, steals, or how many misses they have forced.
timing_constraint: Award the CAM-3 hero close-up to the primary defender on dead balls following consecutive stops (example: 2.2s defender close-up).
plain_english_tip: Dunk & Block: Slamming the ball directly through the rim, or leaping to swat an opponent's shot away.

title: Alley-Oop Pass & Mid-Air Dunk Framing (Showing Both The Passer and The Finisher)
trigger_condition: A teammate throws a high lob pass near the rim and another player jumps, catches the ball in mid-air, and dunks it ('an alley-oop').
editor_action: Keep CAM-1 (Main Wide) Wide through the pass and mid-air slam so viewers see the timing of the play, then cut to CAM-2 (Under-Basket) or CAM-3 (Player Close-Up) framed wide enough to show the dunker and the passer pointing at each other as they jog back on defense.
timing_constraint: Brief post-dunk celebration cut capturing the connection between passer and finisher before returning to wide (example: 1.8s to 2.2s hold).
plain_english_tip: Dunk & Block: Slamming the ball directly through the rim, or leaping to swat an opponent's shot away.

title: Crowd Roar & Arena Decibel Surge Celebration Extension
trigger_condition: A home-team dunk, deep 3-pointer, or game-tying basket causes a massive crowd roar spike on the arena microphones.
editor_action: When the arena crowd erupts, let the emotional moment breathe for the viewer at home. Hold the post-basket CAM-3 (Player Close-Up) Player Close-Up or CAM-4 (Coach & Bench) Crowd/Bench reaction slightly longer than in a quiet gym, provided the opposing team is not pushing a fast break.
timing_constraint: Extend celebration hold during high-decibel crowd surges when transition is slow (example: 2.5s to 3.2s hold vs. 1.5s in a quiet gym; +10 dB audio spike).
plain_english_tip: Fast Break & Press: Sprinting to score before defenders set up, or guarding full-court immediately after a made basket.

title: Sideline Reporter & Courtside Update 'Throw' Window
trigger_condition: Coming out of halftime or the first dead ball after a media timeout, the main announcer throws to the courtside reporter for a brief update on what a coach said in the huddle or an injury check.
editor_action: Show the courtside reporter or coach on CAM-4 (Coach & Bench) briefly at the start of their report so viewers see who is speaking, then cut back to CAM-1 (Main Wide) as soon as the referee hands the ball to the inbounder while letting the reporter finish speaking over live play.
timing_constraint: Brief visual establisher on CAM-4 during the dead ball (example: 4s to 6s), then voice-over on CAM-1 Wide once play resumes.

title: Freshman / Role-Player Unexpected Hero Emergence
trigger_condition: Macro game pattern when a low-scoring role player or freshman scores 8+ unexpected points in a half.
editor_action: Promote the emerging player into the CAM-3 (Player Close-Up) hero rotation and display their season average vs. tonight's point total so viewers appreciate the surprise performance.
timing_constraint: Promote after the player's 3rd made field goal of the half (example: 3.0s CAM-3 + stat note).

title: Exhaustion & Heavy-Minutes Ironman Check-In
trigger_condition: Macro game pattern when a star player has played 35+ minutes without sitting on the bench in a close game.
editor_action: During free throws or dead balls in the final 6 minutes, cut to CAM-3 (Player Close-Up) showing the star player's breathing/posture (hands on knees or towel on shoulders) alongside a 'Minutes Played Tonight' graphic.
timing_constraint: Show during a late-game free-throw walk-up when player minutes >= 35 (example: 3.5s CAM-3 cut).
plain_english_tip: Free Throw: An unguarded 1-point penalty shot from 15 feet while the game clock is stopped.

title: Put-Back Tip-Dunk Overhead Rim Cut (CAM-5 -> CAM-3)
trigger_condition: An offensive player leaps to catch a missed shot in mid-air and slams it straight back through the hoop ('put-back dunk').
editor_action: After the ball goes through the net on CAM-1, punch briefly to CAM-5 (Above-Rim) or CAM-2 (Baseline Low) for 1.0s, then to CAM-3 (Scorer Close-Up) for 1.5s before returning to CAM-1 (Main Wide).
timing_constraint: Quick 2-beat celebration cut on walk-up inbounds (example: 1.0s CAM-5 + 1.5s CAM-3).
plain_english_tip: Dunk & Block: Slamming the ball directly through the rim, or leaping to swat an opponent's shot away.

title: Showing The Coach-Vs-Coach Strategy Battle on The Sidelines
trigger_condition: Macro Game Pattern (Tactical Adjustments Across the Game): Coaches changing how their team defends or calling out plays from the sideline.
editor_action: Allocate roughly 5% to 7% of total broadcast time to CAM-4 (Coach & Bench camera) during dead balls and substitutions to show coaches drawing up plays, signaling defensive changes, or encouraging their players, helping viewers see that basketball is a chess match between coaches as well as players.
timing_constraint: Use brief sideline coach cuts during dead-ball whistles and substitution pauses (example: 2.5s to 3.5s sideline cut).

title: Explaining a 'Held Ball / Jump Ball' Tie-Up and The Possession Arrow
trigger_condition: Two opposing players grab the basketball firmly at the same time and neither can pull it away without fouling ('a held ball' or 'tie-up').
editor_action: Cut briefly to CAM-2 (Baseline Low) or CAM-3 (Player Close-Up) to show the two players wrestling for the ball and the referee signaling a tie-up (thumbs up). In college basketball, teams take turns getting the ball on tie-ups based on the 'possession arrow' at the scorer's table; return to the wide camera and highlight which way the possession arrow is pointing.
timing_constraint: Brief close-up of the tie-up followed by a wide view and possession-arrow note before the throw-in (example: 2.5s tie-up reaction).

title: Showing The Scorer Followed by The Frustrated Opposing Coach
trigger_condition: One team scores several baskets in a row without the other team scoring ('a scoring run'), forcing the opposing coach to call a timeout.
editor_action: Show a close-up of the player who just scored on CAM-3, and immediately follow it with CAM-4 (the sideline camera) showing the opposing coach reacting or calling their players over to regroup.
timing_constraint: Pair the player celebration with the coach's reaction so the viewer immediately sees both sides of the momentum swing (example: 2.2s scorer -> 2.0s coach).

title: Star-Vs-Star Back-To-Back Basket Reactions (Answering Each Other)
trigger_condition: The best scorer on Team A makes a tough basket, and on the very next trip down the floor, the best scorer on Team B answers with a basket of their own.
editor_action: Highlight the personal duel for the audience: show a quick close-up of the scorer on CAM-3 (Player Close-Up) followed by a brief glimpse of the other star or bench on CAM-4 (Coach & Bench) before returning to the wide court view.
timing_constraint: Short back-to-back reaction cuts during normal pace; return immediately to wide if a fast break starts (example: 1.6s scorer -> 1.2s counterpart).
plain_english_tip: Fast Break & Press: Sprinting to score before defenders set up, or guarding full-court immediately after a made basket.

title: Swish Net-Snap Audio Enhancement
trigger_condition: A perimeter jump shot goes cleanly through the hoop without touching the metal rim ('nothing but net'). (Visual cue: The white nylon net whipping upward cleanly on a made three-pointer or mid-range jumper; Audio cue: A crisp cloth 'swish' captured by the under-basket microphone.)
editor_action: Preserve the high-frequency snap of the net microphone in the audio mix on clean perimeter makes, giving the viewer a satisfying sensory confirmation that the shot went in (example: 2 kHz-6 kHz clarity presence on the net mic). Recommended framing: Main Sideline Camera (CAM-1, Main Wide) -> Hero Iso.
timing_constraint: Keep the net mic gated when the ball is not near the basket so crowd chatter behind the hoop does not bleed into the mix (Sync audio transition within <= 0.5s of visual cut; restore live commentary priority before inbound.)
plain_english_tip: 3-Pointer: Any shot released from behind the large painted arc counts for 3 points instead of 2.

title: Post-Entry Subtle Zoom-In for Low-Post Battle
trigger_condition: An offensive team passes the ball into their big man positioned with his back to the basket near the painted area. (Visual cue: Center or power forward sealing his defender on the low block and catching the entry pass; Audio cue: Commentator notes the mismatch or post-up opportunity down low.)
editor_action: Perform a slow, subtle zoom-in (~10-15% tighter) on the main sideline camera so the viewer can see the physical footwork and leverage battle in the post while still keeping the weak-side three-point shooters inside the frame (example: focal tighten over ~1.5s). Recommended framing: Main Sideline Camera (CAM-1, Main Wide).
timing_constraint: Target window: focal tighten over ~1.5s. Ease back out to the full half-court width immediately if the post player kicks the ball back out to the three-point arc.
plain_english_tip: The Paint: The rectangular lane under the hoop where inside scorers battle (offensive players cannot camp inside it for >3 seconds).

title: Shallow Depth-Of-Field Background Blur on Hero Close-Ups
trigger_condition: A star player is shown on CAM-3 (Player Close-Up) after a big basket or during a dead-ball pause. (Visual cue: Long-focal-length telephoto shot of the player from the chest up; Audio cue: Commentator praising the star's performance.)
editor_action: Use a long lens setting that softly blurs the background crowd so the player's facial expression and jersey stand out with cinematic clarity (example: telephoto focal framing isolating the subject from distracted spectators). Recommended framing: Tight Hero Close-Up (CAM-3, Player Close-Up).
timing_constraint: Ensure autofocus or manual follow-focus locks onto the player's eyes before cutting the camera live to air.

title: Foul Perpetrator to Victim Eyeline Bridge
trigger_condition: A defender commits a hard foul on a driving scorer, and both players react during the stoppage. (Visual cue: Scorer picking himself up near the baseline while the defender raises his hands toward the referee; Audio cue: Whistle and commentary discussing the physical contact.)
editor_action: Show the fouled shooter first, then cut to the defender who committed the foul while maintaining consistent camera axis orientation so the viewer clearly understands the two halves of the confrontation (example: ~2.0s on fouled shooter -> ~2.0s on defender). Recommended framing: Hero Iso (CAM-3, Player Close-Up) -> Baseline Close (CAM-2, Baseline Low).
timing_constraint: Target window: ~2.0s on fouled shooter -> ~2.0s on defender. Return to CAM-1 (Main Wide) as soon as the players step up to the free-throw line.
plain_english_tip: Free Throw: An unguarded 1-point penalty shot from 15 feet while the game clock is stopped.

title: Sneaker-Squeak Court-Fx Balance During Half-Court Sets
