trigger_condition: A quiet or mid-tempo half-court possession where the commentary team pauses briefly between sentences. (Visual cue: Players cutting and planting their feet on the hardwood floor; Audio cue: Natural gaps in play-by-play speech lasting more than a second.)
editor_action: Gently raise the floor-level shotgun microphones during commentary pauses so viewers hear the authentic rhythm of sneaker squeaks, ball dribbles, and player communication on the court (example: +3 dB court-FX swell during speech gaps > 1.2s). Recommended framing: Main Sideline Camera (CAM-1, Main Wide).
timing_constraint: Target window: +3 dB court-FX swell during speech gaps > 1.2s. Immediately duck the floor microphones back down the instant an announcer begins speaking so court noise never masks human speech.

title: Handheld Baseline Camera Stabilization During Player Celebrations
trigger_condition: A player scores a physical basket in the paint and walks toward the baseline while celebrating or flexing. (Visual cue: Baseline camera operator walking backward ahead of the celebrating player; Audio cue: Crowd roaring as the game heads to a timeout.)
editor_action: Switch to the handheld baseline camera only once the operator has stabilized their footing and framed the player from the waist up, avoiding jarring footsteps or horizon tilt (example: horizon tilt kept within < 2 degrees). Recommended framing: Baseline Handheld (CAM-2, Baseline Low).
timing_constraint: Target window: horizon tilt kept within < 2 degrees. Cut back to a tripod-mounted camera (CAM-3 (Player Close-Up) or CAM-1 (Main Wide)) immediately if the handheld operator stumbles or gets bumped by a player.
plain_english_tip: The Paint: The rectangular lane under the hoop where inside scorers battle (offensive players cannot camp inside it for >3 seconds).

title: Bench Towel-Wave Framing Without Occluding Court
trigger_condition: Bench players jump up in the foreground on the near sideline after a big three-pointer while play continues on the floor. (Visual cue: Standing substitutes at the bottom edge of CAM-1 (Main Wide); Audio cue: Crowd roar while the opposing team quickly inbounds the ball.)
editor_action: Adjust the vertical tilt of CAM-1 (Main Wide) slightly upward if standing bench players on the near sideline begin blocking the view of the near-side corner or sideline dribble (example: slight +2 degree upward tilt adjustment). Recommended framing: Main Sideline Camera (CAM-1, Main Wide).
timing_constraint: Never cut to a tight bench camera while the ball is actively being dribbled near that sideline (Maintain steady framing for >= 1.5s hold floor and return to CAM-1 before live shot release.)
plain_english_tip: 3-Pointer: Any shot released from behind the large painted arc counts for 3 points instead of 2.

title: Eye-Trace Quadrant Preservation on Hero Cuts
trigger_condition: The director cuts from the wide sideline view (CAM-1, Main Wide) to a tight close-up (CAM-3, Player Close-Up) after a made basket. (Visual cue: The scorer was positioned in the left or right third of the wide frame when the ball went through the net; Audio cue: Announcer calls the scorer's name.)
editor_action: Compose the incoming close-up shot so the player's head and upper body appear near the same horizontal area of the screen where the viewer's eyes were already resting at the end of the wide shot, minimizing eye fatigue (example: eye-trace jump kept within a comfortable central zone). Recommended framing: Main Sideline (CAM-1, Main Wide) -> Tight Hero Close-Up (CAM-3, Player Close-Up).
timing_constraint: Target window: eye-trace jump kept within a comfortable central zone. Avoid cutting from a player on the far-left edge of the wide shot to a close-up where the player is pressed against the far-right edge of the frame.

title: Substitution Scorer's Table to Exiting Player Continuity
trigger_condition: A reserve player checks in at the scorer's table to replace a tired starter during a dead ball. (Visual cue: Substitute standing by the scorer's table waiting for the referee's wave-in; Audio cue: Horn sounds for a substitution.)
editor_action: Show the incoming substitute entering from the scorer's table and clapping hands with the exiting player in a single shot or smooth two-shot sequence so the viewer knows exactly who just entered and who just left the game (example: ~2.5s hand-slap transition shot). Recommended framing: Bench / Table Medium (CAM-4, Coach & Bench) -> Hero Iso (CAM-3, Player Close-Up).
timing_constraint: Target window: ~2.5s hand-slap transition shot. Pair with a small lower-third substitution pill (IN: #X / OUT: #Y) so novices don't have to guess jersey numbers.
plain_english_tip: Two Clocks: Teams have 30 seconds on the shot clock to hit the rim on each possession while the 20-minute half clock counts down.

title: Bench Celebration Mic Swell on Three-Point Makes
trigger_condition: A player hits a three-point shot right in front of their own team's bench. (Visual cue: Reserve players leaping off the bench waving towels near the sideline; Audio cue: Collective roar from the team bench area.)
editor_action: Cross-fade the sideline bench microphone up while cutting to the celebrating bench so the viewer hears the teammates cheering alongside the visual reaction (example: ~1.5s bench audio blend). Recommended framing: Bench Reaction Medium (CAM-4, Coach & Bench).
timing_constraint: Apply a profanity delay buffer or high-pass filter if raw player audio is near the live broadcast threshold.
plain_english_tip: 3-Pointer: Any shot released from behind the large painted arc counts for 3 points instead of 2.

title: Arena PA Organ & Chant Swell During Clutch Defense
trigger_condition: The home crowd chants 'DE-FENSE!' in unison with the arena organ or drumbeat during a late second-half possession. (Visual cue: Home fans standing and clapping in rhythm while their team defends; Audio cue: Rhythmic low-end drum/organ beat and synchronized crowd chant.)
editor_action: Mix the stereo crowd microphones slightly wider and warmer so the home viewer feels the rhythmic stadium pressure building around the offensive team (example: +2.5 dB stereo crowd ambiance during rhythmic chants). Recommended framing: Main Sideline Camera (CAM-1, Main Wide).
timing_constraint: Target window: +2.5 dB stereo crowd ambiance during rhythmic chants. Keep the center channel reserved for the commentators so their voices remain crisp and separated from the crowd chant.

title: Hardwood Ball-Bounce Presence on Iso Dribble
trigger_condition: A star ball-handler clears out one side of the floor and dribbles rhythmically at the top of the key with the shot clock winding down. (Visual cue: Four offensive teammates spaced to the corners while the star dribbles 1-on-1 against a crouched defender; Audio cue: Rhythmic, heavy thumping of the basketball against the wood floor.)
editor_action: Blend in the mid-court shotgun microphone so the viewer hears the rhythmic pulse of the live dribble as the isolation play builds toward the shot (example: subtle +2 dB low-mid presence on court mics). Recommended framing: Main Sideline Camera (CAM-1, Main Wide).
timing_constraint: Target window: subtle +2 dB low-mid presence on court mics. Keep the camera wide on CAM-1 (Main Wide) so the viewer sees both the ball-handler's dribble and the help defenders waiting in the paint.
plain_english_tip: 10-Second Backcourt: The offense has 10 seconds to dribble across the center line and cannot pass back behind it once across.

title: Coach Sideline Pacing Tracking Pan
trigger_condition: During a dead ball or after a controversial call, a head coach walks animatedly along the sideline gesturing to their team or the officials. (Visual cue: Coach moving laterally along the coaching box near the bench; Audio cue: Commentator remarks on the coach's frustration or intensity.)
editor_action: Track the coach with a smooth lateral pan on CAM-4 (Coach & Bench), keeping a slight lead room in the direction the coach is walking so they don't appear to walk into the edge of the screen (example: 60/40 rule-of-thirds lead framing). Recommended framing: Bench Reaction Medium (CAM-4, Coach & Bench).
timing_constraint: Do not hold on the coach once the ball is live and crossing midcourt.
plain_english_tip: 10-Second Backcourt: The offense has 10 seconds to dribble across the center line and cannot pass back behind it once across.

title: Skycam / Overhead Angle Usage for Spacing Breakdowns
trigger_condition: During a timeout or replay sequence, the analyst wants to show how an offense spread the floor or how a zone defense shifted. (Visual cue: High-angle overhead or high-catwalk camera view looking down at the court geometry; Audio cue: Analyst explaining floor spacing, passing lanes, or defensive rotations.)
editor_action: Use the high-angle overhead camera for tactical replays where floor geometry and passing lanes are the main teaching point, giving novices a video-game-like map of the 10 players (example: ~5s overhead replay during a timeout breakdown). Recommended framing: High Overhead / Tactical Replay.
timing_constraint: Target window: ~5s overhead replay during a timeout breakdown. Avoid staying on the overhead angle for prolonged stretches of live play, as it flattens vertical jump height and player facial identity.

title: Rim & Backboard Landmark Anchor in Baseline Cuts
trigger_condition: The broadcast cuts to a low-angle baseline camera (CAM-2 (Baseline Low) or CAM-5 (Above-Rim)) after a drive to the hoop. (Visual cue: Tight view near the baseline after a layup or foul; Audio cue: Whistle or net snap.)
editor_action: Include a recognizable court landmark (such as the rim, backboard stanchion, or painted key line) in the baseline frame so the viewer immediately understands where the camera is positioned relative to the hoop (example: rim or stanchion visible in upper/side frame). Recommended framing: Baseline Close-Up (CAM-2, Baseline Low).
timing_constraint: Avoid disorienting close-ups of just crowd seats and a player's back where no court lines or basket landmarks are visible (Enforce >= 1.5s shot-hold minimum and preserve 180-degree court direction across cuts.)

title: Free-Throw Silence Tension Bed on Road Misses
trigger_condition: A visiting player is at the free-throw line in the final two minutes of a close game while the home crowd waves thundersticks and screams. (Visual cue: Visual wave of motion behind the backboard as the shooter takes a deep breath; Audio cue: Peak high-decibel crowd noise aimed at distracting the shooter.)
editor_action: Hold the full, un-attenuated arena crowd noise for a brief beat before the shooter releases the ball so the viewer experiences the hostile road environment (example: 1.5s ambient crowd showcase before commentary resumes). Recommended framing: Tight Hero Close-Up (CAM-3, Player Close-Up) -> Main Sideline (CAM-1, Main Wide).
timing_constraint: Target window: 1.5s ambient crowd showcase before commentary resumes. Ensure commentary microphones have strong noise-rejection gates so the crowd roar does not bleed doubly through the announcers' headsets.
plain_english_tip: Free Throw: An unguarded 1-point penalty shot from 15 feet while the game clock is stopped.

title: Rule-Of-Thirds Look-Space on Player Interviews & Reactions
trigger_condition: A player on the court or bench is looking strongly to the left or right of the screen toward the scoreboard, referee, or teammate. (Visual cue: Player's head and gaze directed toward one side of the frame; Audio cue: Dead-ball commentary discussion.)
editor_action: Position the player slightly off-center so there is open visual space ('look room') in the direction their eyes are facing, making the composition feel natural and balanced (example: subject eyes placed near the upper one-third line with look-space ahead). Recommended framing: Tight Hero Close-Up (CAM-3, Player Close-Up).
timing_constraint: Re-center the frame if the player turns to face straight ahead (Maintain steady framing for >= 1.5s hold floor and return to CAM-1 before live shot release.)

title: 360-Degree Replay Orbit Axis Return
trigger_condition: A specialized multi-camera 'bullet-time' or 360-degree replay sweeps around the basket during a highlight replay. (Visual cue: Camera viewpoint rotating around a frozen or slow-motion dunk; Audio cue: Analyst marveling at the hang-time of the play.)
editor_action: Ensure the rotating replay finishes its sweep facing back toward the standard sideline orientation or uses a clean graphic wipe before returning to live action on CAM-1 (Main Wide) so the viewer's spatial sense of the court is smoothly restored (example: ~0.3s wipe transition back to live sideline axis). Recommended framing: Multi-Angle Replay -> Main Sideline (CAM-1, Main Wide).
timing_constraint: Target window: ~0.3s wipe transition back to live sideline axis. Limit rotating or reverse-axis replays to major stoppages (timeouts or half ends).
plain_english_tip: Dunk & Block: Slamming the ball directly through the rim, or leaping to swat an opponent's shot away.

title: Player On-Court Communication Isolation During Dead Balls
trigger_condition: Two teammates huddle near midcourt to discuss defensive switches while waiting for a free throw or inbound pass. (Visual cue: Players pointing at assignments and talking with their hands covering their mouths or gesturing; Audio cue: Quiet commentary moment during a routine stoppage.)
editor_action: Cut to a medium two-shot of the communicating teammates while the analyst explains what defensive adjustment they are making, keeping court audio low enough to avoid airing stray profanity (example: -12 dB court parabolic mic pad during close-up). Recommended framing: Tight Hero Close-Up (CAM-3, Player Close-Up).
timing_constraint: Target window: -12 dB court parabolic mic pad during close-up. Cut away immediately if the conversation turns into an heated argument with an official that risks broadcasting audible profanity.
plain_english_tip: 10-Second Backcourt: The offense has 10 seconds to dribble across the center line and cannot pass back behind it once across.

title: Wet-Spot Floor Mopping Delay Coverage
trigger_condition: Referees pause play for 10 to 20 seconds so arena attendants can mop sweat off the court after a player slips.
editor_action: Use the floor-mopping pause to show CAM-4 (Coach & Bench) coach instructions at the sideline or roll a queued highlight replay, returning to CAM-1 (Main Wide) as the attendant steps off the court.
timing_constraint: Fill the 10s to 20s mop delay with CAM-4 or replay, returning to CAM-1 2.0s before throw-in.
plain_english_tip: Offensive Rebound: Catching your own team's missed shot resets the NCAA shot clock to 20 seconds for an extra scoring chance.

title: Celebrity, Alumni, or Mascot Crowd Cut During Extended Stoppages Only
trigger_condition: A notable school alumnus, celebrity, or energetic mascot is spotted in the stands by an isolation camera.
editor_action: Only air crowd or alumni cutaways on CAM-4 (Coach & Bench) during extended dead-ball stoppages (free-throw setups, official reviews, or coming out of timeouts); never cut to the crowd during live play.
timing_constraint: Restrict crowd/alumni cuts to dead-ball windows >= 5.0s.
plain_english_tip: Free Throw: An unguarded 1-point penalty shot from 15 feet while the game clock is stopped.

title: Senior Night / Nba Draft Prospect Spotlight Continuity
trigger_condition: Macro game pattern when a marquee senior or top pro prospect is featured in pre-game storylines.
editor_action: Check in on the featured player on CAM-3 (Player Close-Up) at least once per 8-minute game segment (after a key basket, rebound, or huddle instruction) to keep the pre-game narrative thread alive.
timing_constraint: 1 spotlight check-in every ~8 game minutes on dead balls (example: 3.5s iso).
plain_english_tip: Offensive Rebound: Catching your own team's missed shot resets the NCAA shot clock to 20 seconds for an extra scoring chance.

title: Assist-Passer Point-And-Acknowledge Cut
trigger_condition: A guard delivers a no-look or cross-court pass that leads to an easy layup or dunk, and the scorer points back to thank the passer.
editor_action: On a slow opponent walk-up, split the post-basket celebration between the scorer on CAM-2 (Baseline Low) and the passer on CAM-3 (or frame both together if running back side-by-side).
timing_constraint: Brief post-basket acknowledgement cut before the ball crosses mid-court (example: 2.0s).
plain_english_tip: 10-Second Backcourt: The offense has 10 seconds to dribble across the center line and cannot pass back behind it once across.
